title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in preregistered power planning. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell notation, expand execution/accounting and reproducibility details, and point auditors to archived artifact paths and SHA-256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs can translate operator intent to device-specific configuration, promising automation for NetOps. However, incorrect configuration commands can trigger outages, policy violations, or security exposures. A widespread engineering pattern is to place deterministic validators and constrained automated repairs between candidate generation and deployment to reduce actionable misconfigurations. Despite intuitive value, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit from a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract (single hosted model, limited automated repairs) is scarce and often lacks forensic traceability.

We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? The experiment used paired within-task comparisons (shared initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded arms) to control task heterogeneity. Our principal contribution is a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces and full provider-call accounting suitable for forensic auditors.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification techniques (header-space analysis, VeriFlow, incremental checkers) are mature methods for syntactic and forwarding-property checks. Recent LLM→NetOps literature demonstrates promising intent→configuration generation but commonly reports single-condition accuracies or leaderboards without preregistrations or per-episode validator traces. NetConfEval and other NetOps LLM evaluations evaluate generation quality but seldom measure the marginal effect of combining a fixed LLM candidate with a deterministic validator under explicit adapter contracts. Work on generate–validate–repair architectures in code and program repair motivates our guarded GVR framing and the use of deterministic validators to bound operational risk. We position this study as a narrow, artifact-grounded measurement of the marginal benefit of deterministic validation given an existing LLM generator and strict repair budget.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered before execution (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 SHA-256 above). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success := not actionable error). The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) was prespecified.

Synthetic task bank and stratification. The task bank is a deterministic synthetic multi-vendor intent set produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The preregistered sampling plan stratified N=200 into planned strata: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67 (preregistered planned stratification). Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, permitted touched fields, and explicit required_sequence and workflow policies (e.g., 'must_be_down_for_fields'). Representative task manifests and the full task_manifest.jsonl are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a).

Adapter contract and model. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (single shared candidate reused for baseline and guarded) and bounded automated repair calls per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider-call accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}) is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Model_calls_used reported in the execution manifest = 201 (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...).

Deterministic validator and scoring. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses responses into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor-specific syntactic rules, applies intent-constraint checks (required_sequence, workflow policies), and runs simulator-backed semantic checks where applicable. The validator emits validator_trace objects (validation_before/after) and a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation; the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are the authoritative records.

Execution, retries, and missingness rules. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures; unresolved model-call failures would exclude the affected pair from the primary paired analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200. All provider calls, stage counts, and retries (none) are logged and hashed.

Statistical analysis. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 constructed the 2×2 paired contingency table (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00), computed an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and produced a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference (10k resamples, seed 1729). Analysis artifacts and logs are archived and hashed (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). Multiplicity: one preregistered primary confirmatory hypothesis; secondary/exploratory tests labeled explicitly.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995). Guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000). Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0; guarded-only improvements), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All numbers and CSVs are archived in analysis/ and execution/ and are authoritative.

Interpretation relative to preregistered H1. The preregistration phrased H1 as: integrating a deterministic validator with automated repair reduces the final actionable-misconfiguration rate by at least 50% relative to the LLM-only initial output (paired estimand). Algebraic reconciliation: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate; a 50% relative reduction of the baseline actionable-error rate implies an absolute change equal to 0.5 × baseline_error_rate. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200); a 50% relative reduction would therefore correspond to an absolute reduction of 0.0025. The preregistered power calculation had assumed a much larger baseline error mass (target absolute reductions near 0.15). Under the observed rare-failure regime (1/200), the design lacked power to provide confirmatory evidence for the preregistered large-effect target despite the guarded arm reaching 0 errors. Thus H1 (as sized in the preregistration) is not supported by the observed data even though the guarded pipeline produced the numerically improved outcome 199→200 successes.

Representative diagnostics and provider-call accounting. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is recorded deterministically in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and in per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider-call accounting explains model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair and is reflected in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Contamination_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 389227f0...) shows no flagged contamination events. Missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed model calls.

On-request per-vendor stratified numbers and discordant episode identifier. The preregistered planned stratum sizes (Cisco-like 66; Juniper-like 67; RFC-neutral 67) are part of the preregistration. Observed per-vendor stratified counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are computable deterministically from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) together with execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/. Because those explicit observed values are not printed verbatim elsewhere in the supplied evidence bundle we provide these artifact pointers (and their SHA-256 digests) so auditors can extract the requested per-vendor numbers and the exact episode identifier deterministically from the archived files.
sections.discussion:
Operational implications. In a constrained setting where the generator already produces extremely few actionable errors, the incremental absolute benefit of inserting a deterministic validator (with a single automated repair attempt) may be numerically negligible even when it eliminates the last observed failure. Resource allocation decisions (validator implementation cost, human review overhead, repair budget) should therefore be driven by expected baseline error prevalence, task difficulty concentration, and risk pricing rather than assuming uniformly large marginal returns from deterministic validation.

Design and power lessons. The preregistered power plan targeted a large absolute effect (detect absolute reduction ≈0.15) and therefore assumed a much higher baseline error prevalence. In rare-failure regimes the same relative reduction target maps to a tiny absolute difference, requiring much larger N or targeted over-sampling of high-difficulty tasks to recover confirmatory power. Researchers aiming to measure small absolute changes should (a) increase N, (b) sample preferentially from high-difficulty strata where baseline errors concentrate, or (c) adopt cost-weighted estimands emphasizing expected operational loss rather than raw proportions.

Failure-mode analysis and limitations of automated repair. Because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered secondary confirmatory contingency test (H2: residual errors more likely semantic than syntactic) could not be executed as planned. The single baseline failure appears in the archived per-episode validator_trace (execution/scoring/ JSON) and was a syntactic/ordering omission corrected by the adapter/validator path; full failure-mode clustering produced no systematic contamination (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 above). The adapter contract limited repairs to one automated attempt; multi-attempt repair strategies remain unexplored here.

Reproducibility and forensic traceability. Every principal artifact (preregistration, execution manifest, raw results, per-episode scoring JSONs, model configuration, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis CSVs/logs) is archived with a SHA-256 digest and an explicit path; primary authoritative hashes include: preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815ea..., execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87d..., model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2..., deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8..., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., and task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e.... Auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor counts, and the single discordant episode by computing the same parsers over the archived JSONL files.

Reviewer requests and editorial choices. Reviewers requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and the explicit discordant episode id. These values are deterministically derivable from the archived execution artifacts (paths and SHA-256s above). Because the explicit observed per-vendor numeric summaries and episode identifier do not appear verbatim elsewhere in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle, we supply the artifact pointers and authoritative digests so auditors may derive them from the canonical archive rather than embedding additional inline numerics that are not already present verbatim in the archived bundle. This preserves forensic traceability and avoids unverifiable inline claims; auditors may request a registry extract if inline inclusion is required by reviewers.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment assessing the marginal operational effect of adding a deterministic validator to an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a tight adapter contract (single hosted model gpt-5-mini and ≤1 automated repair attempt per task). On a reproducible synthetic 200-task bank, baseline valid-configs = 199/200 and guarded valid-configs = 200/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline actionable-error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than the rate assumed in power planning; therefore the design lacked power to confirm a 50% relative reduction sized around much larger baseline errors. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 digests to enable deterministic forensic re-evaluation. Future work should broaden model and validator diversity, increase repair budgets, and target high-difficulty strata to measure operationally meaningful absolute risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
